label: Velexis
description: Velexis is a multi-tenant flight-booking system: a platform (control plane) that sells and runs OTAs, and the OTA product each of them runs on, built on shared packages and deployed to one VM.

children.label: Platform (control plane)
children.description: The Velexis side that treats OTAs as customers: the portal, the platform admin console and the platform API with its worker.

children.label: Identity and access
children.description: Who may use the portal and the admin console, how they prove it, and how a member reaches an OTA's back office.

children.label: Accounts, sign-in and sessions
children.description: Portal accounts, password sign-in with lockout, e-mailed token links and refresh-token sessions.

children.label: MFA and step-up
children.description: TOTP two-factor sign-in, recovery codes, mandatory enrolment and fresh codes before sensitive actions.

children.label: Platform admin access
children.description: How Velexis staff become platform admins and how the admin console guards its session and routes.

children.label: OTA teams and roles
children.description: Memberships, invitations and the five tenant roles that decide what each member may do for an OTA.

children.label: Console single sign-on
children.description: Opening an OTA's back office from the portal with a single-use portal token posted to the OTA admin.

children.label: Tenancy and provisioning
children.description: Creating, configuring, suspending and launching OTAs (tenants), from the first schema to the live switch.

children.label: Tenants and tenant keys
children.description: An OTA as a row of `platform.tenants` and the short key that names its schema and sub-domain.

children.label: Provisioning pipeline
children.description: The durable job that has the OTA worker create a tenant schema, the platform's follow-up steps and the setup page that tracks it.

children.label: Suspension and tenant maintenance
children.description: Suspending and resuming an OTA and re-running its tenant migrations through provisioning jobs.

children.label: Custom domains
children.description: Customer-owned storefront hosts, their DNS verification and the TLS ask endpoint Caddy consults.

children.label: Environments and go-live
children.description: Each OTA's test or live storefront environment and the preconditions of the one-way switch to live.

children.label: Billing and subscriptions
children.description: What OTAs pay Velexis, how Stripe Billing keeps that in sync, and what Velexis pays out to OTAs.

children.label: Plans and subscriptions
children.description: Plans with limits and features, each tenant's subscription state and the billing notices it raises.

children.label: Stripe Billing and events
children.description: Stripe Checkout, the Customer Portal and the verified webhook inbox that keep subscriptions in step with Stripe.

children.label: Settlements and payouts
children.description: Monthly statements of Velexis-collected payments owed to OTAs and the bank accounts they are paid to.

children.label: Supplier and payment connections
children.description: How each OTA is connected to Amadeus (shared Velexis offices or its own credentials) and to Stripe.

children.label: Amadeus connections
children.description: Per-environment supplier connections, the shared Velexis Amadeus account, own-credential submissions and live access requests.

children.label: Amadeus office pool
children.description: The pool of Velexis Amadeus offices assigned to OTAs and released when no future travel remains.

children.label: Payment connections
children.description: Which Stripe account takes an OTA's customer payments, Stripe Connect Standard and the card statement suffix.

children.label: Back office and platform operations
children.description: The Velexis staff console, its audit trail, and the platform worker that runs queues and schedules behind it.

children.label: Platform admin console
children.description: The staff console's home dashboard and shell from which admins run the fleet of OTAs.

children.label: Audit and accountability
children.description: Mandatory reasons on admin actions, the platform audit log and its bounded CSV export.

children.label: Platform worker and schedules
children.description: The platform backend's second process and the cron schedules it runs in UTC.

children.label: Portal experience
children.description: Patterns of the portal UI that every OTA page shares: banners, checklists, error wording and one-time secrets.

children.label: OTA product
children.description: The data plane every OTA runs on: the booking API and worker, the hosted storefront, the OTA admin and the JavaScript SDK.

children.label: Travel content and Amadeus
children.description: Everything that comes from Amadeus: access and rate limits, flight search and pricing, and the supplier log and queues.

children.label: Amadeus access
children.description: The Amadeus Enterprise operations, cached OAuth tokens, call rate limits and the remark Velexis writes into orders.

children.label: Search, offers and pricing
children.description: Flight searches, their offers, branded fare upsells and the priced offer that starts a checkout.

children.label: Supplier log and Amadeus queues
children.description: The redacted record of every Amadeus call and the polled snapshots of the OTA's Amadeus queues.

children.label: Booking lifecycle
children.description: From a checkout to a ticketed booking and beyond: orders, ticketing, timeouts and reconciliation, e-mails and documents.

children.label: Checkout
children.description: The purchase in progress and the traveller details the airline requires for the chosen fare.

children.label: Bookings and self-service
children.description: Bookings with their references, the self-service actions and cancellation modes they allow, and periodic sync with Amadeus.

children.label: Ticketing
children.description: When and whether tickets are issued: the OTA's ticketing policy, ticketing status and unpaid issue.

children.label: Supplier timeouts and reconciliation
children.description: What happens when Amadeus does not answer an order readably: pending bookings, reconciliation and staff review.

children.label: Notifications and documents
children.description: Booking e-mails from per-locale templates, alerts to the OTA's staff and the PDF itinerary and e-tickets.

children.label: Payments and PCI
children.description: How a traveller's price is built and paid (Stripe card or airline card) and how card data stays inside PCI scope.

children.label: Pricing, markups and fees
children.description: Net Amadeus prices, the OTA's markup and fee rules, and the pricing mode that turns them into a selling price.

children.label: Stripe card payments
children.description: The payment gateway behind which the OTA API hides Stripe: PaymentIntents, the Payment Element, 3-D Secure and webhooks.

children.label: Airline card payments
children.description: Passing the traveller's card in memory only to Amadeus, from an isolated page, with redaction at every step.

children.label: PCI scope and evidence
children.description: Which parts of the system see card data, the cardholder data environment and the evidence kept for PCI DSS.

children.label: Travellers and sessions
children.description: Traveller accounts of one OTA, their sessions and the guest access to a booking without an account.

children.label: Customer accounts and sessions
children.description: Per-OTA traveller accounts, their rotating refresh-token sessions and the erasure of deleted accounts.

children.label: Guest access
children.description: Finding a booking by reference and last name and the guest token cookie that grants access to it.

children.label: Storefront experience
children.description: The hosted multi-tenant storefront: how a page boots for an OTA, what travellers see, and how each OTA brands it.

children.label: Hosting and boot
children.description: One static build serving every OTA: host resolution, runtime configuration, boot and the test-mode banner.

children.label: Pages and interaction
children.description: Shared storefront UI behaviour: header controls, checkout steps, price hold, confirmation, error states and announcements.

children.label: Settings, branding and content
children.description: Each OTA's storefront settings, theme with its contrast fallback, own content pages and uploaded assets.

children.label: Back office (OTA admin)
children.description: The OTA admin where an OTA's staff work bookings, payments and settings through the console operations of the OTA API.

children.label: Console workspace
children.description: The OTA admin's screens and controls: saved views, confirm dialogs, the TEST/LIVE switch, shopping and PNR import.

children.label: Console operations and audit
children.description: The `/v1/console/**` operations, raw Amadeus reads limited to the OTA's offices, and the staff action trail.

children.label: Staff sessions and permissions
children.description: Console sessions, staff roles and their fourteen permissions, and the Redis deny stamps that end staff sessions early.

children.label: SDK and integrations
children.description: How frontends and third parties call the OTA API: API keys, the JavaScript SDK, its session modes and its contract.

children.label: API keys
children.description: Publishable, secret, hosting and console automation keys, their scopes and the one-time reveal of the first keys.

children.label: SDK client
children.description: The client factory, its request core and generated route table, per-call options and the escape hatch.

children.label: SDK session modes
children.description: Cookie, token and server modes, how tokens are supplied and stored, and automatic refresh with its rotation window.

children.label: Errors, retries and paging
children.description: The SDK's typed errors, its retry policy with Retry-After, and cursor pagination of list operations.

children.label: Contract conformance
children.description: The frozen SDK contract, the tests that hold the code to it, and the documented additions, deferrals and deviations.

children.label: Builds and publishing
children.description: The ESM and IIFE bundles and the draft npm publishing workflow with trusted publishing.

children.label: Shared foundation
children.description: What both products share: API conventions, PostgreSQL and Redis, application security controls and queues, mostly from packages/*.

children.label: API contracts and conventions
children.description: The contract-first OpenAPI documents and the conventions every Velexis API follows on the wire.

children.label: OpenAPI contracts
children.description: The generated operations index, each operation's scope and the test that keeps routes and documents in step.

children.label: Error model
children.description: One error envelope with stable codes, field errors and a generated catalogue, thrown as `AppError` by both backends.

children.label: Wire and data conventions
children.description: Idempotency keys, optimistic concurrency with If-Match, prefixed ids and money as decimal strings.

children.label: Data and storage
children.description: PostgreSQL schemas and roles, tenant isolation through tenantTx, migrations, reference data, Redis and file storage.

children.label: Schemas, roles and types
children.description: The platform and reference schemas, the database roles, the platform Kysely instance, type parsers and generated table types.

children.label: Tenant schemas and tenantTx
children.description: One PostgreSQL schema per OTA, reached only through `tenantTx`, with a guard against leaked search paths and a hook that commits seeds with a new schema.

children.label: Migrations
children.description: The one migration runner, its ledgers and reports, expand-and-contract rules and the fan-out over tenant schemas.

children.label: Reference data
children.description: The committed CSV snapshot of airports, airlines and other reference tables, its overrides and its loader.

children.label: Redis and cache invalidation
children.description: Redis kept without eviction for BullMQ, and the pub/sub channel that invalidates rows the OTA backend caches.

children.label: File storage and signed URLs
children.description: The file store for documents and uploads and the short-lived signed links that serve them.

children.label: Security controls
children.description: Application-level protections shared by the apps: encryption and keys, redaction, browser session security and trust between services.

children.label: Encryption and keys
children.description: Envelope encryption under a master key (KEK) kept outside the database, key files, rotation and the API key pepper.

children.label: Redaction and secret display
children.description: Censoring secrets and personal data in logs and stored payloads, and showing secrets masked or only once.

children.label: Cookies, CSRF, CSP and redirects
children.description: `__Host-` cookies, the double-submit CSRF token, content security policies and safe return paths.

children.label: Trust between services
children.description: The shared secrets and headers by which BFF servers, the edge and the OTA admin identify themselves and the end user.

children.label: Queues and background work
children.description: BullMQ queues, the messages the two backends exchange, and the inbox and outbox patterns that make delivery reliable.

children.label: Queues and jobs
children.description: BullMQ queues of the platform and OTA workers (watched from the platform admin console) and the scheduled fan-out of per-tenant jobs.

children.label: Cross-backend messaging
children.description: The two queues on which the platform and the OTA worker ask and answer, and the common job envelope.

children.label: Inbox and outbox
children.description: E-mails written in the same transaction as the change, and incoming webhooks stored once before processing.

children.label: Operations and delivery
children.description: Running Velexis in production on one hardened Ubuntu VM: deployment, the edge, host security, monitoring and backups.

children.label: Deployment and VM
children.description: The single VM, how it is provisioned and checked, how processes are isolated, and how a release is installed or rolled back.

children.label: VM provisioning
children.description: The single-VM design, idempotent provisioning, the read-only hardening check and the pinned Node.js major.

children.label: Trust zones and units
children.description: One system user per trust zone, sandboxed systemd units, root-only env files and one-off commands.

children.label: Releases and deploys
children.description: Self-contained release folders with checksums, the root-owned deploy command, its SSH user and automatic rollback.

children.label: Edge and network
children.description: Caddy at the edge with TLS and the Coraza WAF, and the outbound allow-list that limits where the VM may connect.

children.label: Caddy and TLS
children.description: The Caddy build and service set-up, its admin socket, on-demand TLS for storefront hosts and log filtering.

children.label: Web application firewall
children.description: Coraza with the OWASP Core Rule Set inside Caddy, its narrow exclusions and the detection-only week before blocking.

children.label: Outbound allow-list
children.description: The nftables egress table that drops all output except allowed hosts, and time-limited emergency openings.

children.label: Host security
children.description: Hardening and monitoring of the VM itself: SSH access, file integrity, the audit daemon and security log handling.

children.label: SSH access and file integrity
children.description: A second factor for admin SSH, AIDE file-integrity checks with their baseline and auditd watch rules.

children.label: Security logs
children.description: Hourly encrypted shipment of security log entries off the VM and their hourly review with immediate alerts.

children.label: Observability and alerting
children.description: How problems surface: health checks and failure alerts on the VM, and request ids that tie responses to log lines.

children.label: Health checks and alerts
children.description: The five-minute on-VM health check and the root-owned mailer every failing unit and check reports through.

children.label: Request tracing
children.description: The request id on every response, error and log line, and the SDK hook that reports each response.

children.label: Backups and recovery
children.description: Nightly encrypted backup sets kept off-site and the rehearsed restore that proves they work.

children.label: Engineering practice
children.description: How Velexis is built and changed: architecture patterns, local development, tests and CI, and the rules and plans agents follow.

children.label: Architecture and patterns
children.description: The overall shape of the system and the patterns the apps share for frontends and configuration.

children.label: System shape
children.description: The control plane versus the OTA data plane, Next.js backends-for-frontend and their server actions.

children.label: Configuration and feature switches
children.description: The typed configuration loader every app uses and the feature switches that stay off by default.

children.label: Local development
children.description: Running the whole stack on a laptop: databases, keys, seed data, local doubles for e-mail, Stripe and Amadeus.

children.label: Local stack and seed data
children.description: One-time PostgreSQL and Redis set-up, development keys, the seed with its demo OTA, Mailpit, the Stripe CLI and the Vite proxy.

children.label: Amadeus stub
children.description: The local Amadeus double with recorded fixtures, selectable failure scenarios and in-memory orders.

children.label: CI/CD and testing
children.description: The test layers from unit to end-to-end, performance budgets, and the GitHub workflows that run them and deploy.

children.label: Unit and integration tests
children.description: Template databases, test roles, per-worker Redis, a fake clock, OpenAPI response checks and signed Stripe events.

children.label: End-to-end tests
children.description: The Playwright stack on a fresh database, its projects per app and the storefront's automatic guards.

children.label: SDK tests
children.description: Offline SDK tests with a fake fetch and smoke tests against a running OTA API.

children.label: Performance and size budgets
children.description: The storefront's per-page budgets, the SDK bundle size limit and the platform API smoke test.

children.label: CI and deploy workflows
children.description: The CI, E2E and manual Deploy workflows of GitHub Actions and the production environment that holds deploy secrets.

children.label: Process and governance
children.description: The rules the repository enforces on itself, the agent task plans and contract-first workflow, and compliance bookkeeping.

children.label: Repository rules
children.description: CI checks that refuse hard-coded hosts, version ranges and unpinned Actions, session-level search paths, edits to frozen contract files and focused tests.

children.label: Plans and contract-first workflow
children.description: The linter of the agent task plans and the commands that lint OpenAPI documents and regenerate types.

children.label: Compliance and legal bookkeeping
children.description: Keeping PCI evidence references pointing at the right lines and recording which terms of service a user accepted.
